minutes.headline: Sewer Commission tabled the budget to Feb 15, voted to cut the reconnection fee from $1,000 to $100, and began grease trap non-compliance action.
minutes.summary: The commission postponed the draft FY23 sewer budget to a budget-only meeting the following Tuesday. It spent most of the evening on a list of sewer bylaw and regulation changes ahead of town meeting, voting on a few, and discussed ARPA funding, grease trap compliance, and the annual report.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member checked the purchase of services total in the draft budget against the updated copy.
The DPW director said ARPA general-use funds appear easier to use for sewer projects than first thought, including pump stations and I&I work.
Flow assessment agreed to another year of leasing, maintenance and calibration at the same price, avoiding a bid.
The current minimum charge was mentioned during discussion of prorating bills for new owners.

budget_items.topic: Fixed charge for homes on wells
budget_items.what_was_said: Homes on wells pay a fixed amount based on a set volume; options like per-bedroom pricing were discussed.
The fee to reconnect an already-connected property was considered arbitrary and too high and was reduced by motion.
The draft budget charges annual fees only to non-compliant accounts; revenue lines were given for that versus charging all.
The business manager proposed a letter with a 30-day deadline followed by a daily charge if the report is not filed.
The commission expects budget, capital reserve transfer, OPEB transfer, sewer use regulation and bylaw articles for town meeting.

transfers.description: Normal annual transfers to capital reserve and OPEB planned as town meeting articles

decisions.decision: A budget-only meeting set for Tuesday February 15, time to be set by email (5, 5:30 or 6).
Consensus to allow sewer easements on a case-by-case hardship basis, to be run past town counsel.
Bylaw hearing process (one hearing, posting requirement, televising) to be taken to counsel before any vote.
Business manager to draft grease trap language on inspection charges for non-compliant owners and run it by counsel.
No votes on the policy list items; changes to go to counsel on the 24th.
Annual report to be submitted this week with the typo corrected.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to cut the fee for reconnecting an already-connected property from a thousand dollars to a hundred dollars.
The draft FY23 sewer budget was tabled to a budget-only meeting set for Tuesday, February 15, with the time to be set by email.
The commission voted to start the non-compliance process against the owner of the Crossroads grease interceptor.
It voted to remove a bylaw paragraph that refers to a monitoring and inspection fee system that does not exist.
Most other bylaw and policy changes were not voted. Hearing-process changes and grease trap inspection charges go to town counsel first.

why_it_matters: The reconnection fee change lowers a one-time charge on sewer properties, and the sewer budget that sets user charges is still undecided.
Several bylaw and regulation changes are expected as warrant articles at town meeting, so residents will be asked to vote on them after counsel's review.
watch_next: The budget-only meeting on Tuesday, February 15, where the draft FY23 sewer budget returns.
Town counsel's review of the policy and bylaw changes, scheduled for the 24th, before the town meeting warrant articles.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the four main votes, the reconnection fee, the $107 minimum and the Crossroads penalties. They differ on three points: the official minutes record a 3-0 vote to accept the FY21 annual report that ours does not, the hearing-process item reads as agreed in the official and as pending counsel in ours, and ours names Bob as chair where the official has Dave MacDonald. The 212-versus-"approximately $200" well charge is also worth a look.
